name: Oxybutynin topical gel (OG05009)
question: Does once-daily oxybutynin chloride topical gel reduce urinary incontinence episodes more than placebo gel in adults with overactive bladder and urgency-predominant incontinence?

design.population: Adults with urgency-predominant urinary incontinence and overactive bladder, at least 8 voids and 4 urge incontinence episodes daily, mean voided volume of 350 mL or less, and PVR of 250 mL or less; 704 of 789 randomized participants were women and mean age was 59 years.
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1765; Table 1, p 1766

verdictNote: Daily urinary incontinence episodes declined more with oxybutynin gel at study end.
takeaway: Once-daily oxybutynin chloride 10% topical gel reduced daily urinary incontinence episodes more than placebo gel over 12 weeks in adults with urgency-predominant incontinence (mean change −3.0 versus −2.5 episodes/day; P < 0.0001).

reports.label: 12-week primary report
reports.citation: Staskin DR, Dmochowski RR, Sand PK, et al. "Efficacy and safety of oxybutynin chloride topical gel for overactive bladder: a randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, multicenter study." *J Urol.* 2009;181(4):1764-1772. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2008.11.125

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in daily urinary incontinence episodes at study end (week 12 or last observation)
results.note: Three-day diaries counted urgency and/or stress incontinence; modified intent-to-treat ANCOVA with last observation carried forward. Baseline: 5.4 episodes/day in each arm; study end: 2.4 vs 2.9. The paper gives no adjusted between-arm estimate or confidence interval.
results.locator: Full text, Study Design and Statistical Analysis, pp 1766-1767; Table 2, p 1768

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in daily urinary frequency at study end
Mean change from baseline in voided volume at study end
Mean change from baseline in daily nocturia episodes at study end
results.note: Between-arm difference was not statistically significant.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Efficacy, pp 1768-1769

results.measure: No urinary incontinence episodes on the study-end 3-day diary
results.note: The paper reports no confidence interval or P value for this endpoint.
results.locator: Full text, Study Design, p 1766; Efficacy, p 1768

harms.label: Application-site reactions
harms.note: Skin reactions caused withdrawal in 3/389 (0.8%) vs 1/400 (0.3%).

harms.label: Serious treatment-related adverse events
harms.note: Serious adverse events of any attribution occurred in 7/389 (1.8%) vs 10/400 (2.5%); none were treatment related.

harms.label: Any adverse event
harms.note: Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 73/389 (18.8%) vs 45/400 (11.3%).

harms.label: Treatment-related urinary retention
harms.locator: Full text, Table 4, p 1770; Safety, p 1769
harms.note: At study end, PVR was 250 mL or greater in one patient in each arm.

delivery.label: Treatment regimen
delivery.value: 1 g of 10% oxybutynin chloride topical gel or matching placebo once daily for 12 weeks, applied to rotating sites on the abdomen, upper arm or shoulder, and thigh.

delivery.label: Treatment completion and compliance
delivery.locator: Full text, Results and Figure 2, p 1767
delivery.note: Compliance was assessed by counting unused sachets at each visit.
